images.name: cover
images.title: An *AI Scheduling Assistant* runs the calendar
images.sub: Booking, rescheduling, reminders, waitlists and dispatch: what it owns, what stays with a person, and what the job costs.

images.name: duties
images.title: The scheduling job, *duty by duty*
rows: Reads requests from email, text, calls and forms, offers times that fit the rules and books the one the client picks.
Offers new times, applies the cancellation policy as written and works through a full day when staff are out.
Confirms each booking, sends reminders with what to bring and handles replies like running late.
Offers every cancelled slot to the next person on the waitlist who fits, until someone takes it.
Matches visits to staff by skill and availability, groups them by area and warns clients when a visit runs long.
Requests to waive a fee or book into blocked time are prepared and held for a person.

images.name: day-on-shift
images.title: A day at a *physiotherapy clinic*
rows: A practitioner calls in sick with six patients booked. Moves four to colleagues, two choose next week.
Offers the two open slots to the waitlist. Both are taken by 8:20.
Books the two overnight email requests and texts the web form patient to fix their number.
A patient asks to skip the late cancellation fee. Held for the manager.
A referral mentions a recent fall. Details sent to the manager before booking.
Sends tomorrow's reminders with intake forms for three new patients.
Emails the manager tomorrow's schedule with one unconfirmed booking marked.

images.name: setup
images.title: Setting up an *AI Scheduling Assistant*
steps: Go through real bookings with whoever runs the schedule and ask why each one went where it did.
Appointment types, lengths, who can do what, what clients need first and the cancellation policy.
Booking system, staff calendars, email and text, with only the access the job needs.
It prepares each booking and change, and a person approves them for the first couple of weeks.
Hand over one duty at a time
Reminders first, then new bookings, then rescheduling. Staff-out days come last.
Someone reads the log and updates the rules when staff or services change.
